name: Ireland — PAYE, USC and PRSI

changelog.summary: States what the template leaves out for leave: statutory sick pay (Sick Leave Act 2022) is not calculated. Calculations are unchanged.

Corrects errors: on the emergency basis USC is now 8 % of all pay even when a USC exemption status is set (Employers' Guide 9.5.1); week 53 (pay day 31 December) is calculated on the week 1 basis (14.3) instead of being refused.

2026: PAYE 20 % / 40 % from the RPN on the cumulative, week 1/month 1 or emergency basis; USC 0.5 / 2 / 3 / 8 % (Finance Act 2025); Class A PRSI 4.2 % rising to 4.35 % on 1 October 2026 with the PRSI credit; employer 9 % / 11.25 % rising to 9.15 % / 11.4 % (incl. 1 % NTF levy), threshold €552 a week.

employee.description: Basis of deduction from the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN): cumulative, week 1/month 1, or emergency (with or without a PPS number when no RPN is available)
Yearly standard rate cut-off point from the RPN (required on the cumulative and week 1/month 1 bases)
Yearly tax credits from the RPN (required on the cumulative and week 1/month 1 bases)

USC status from the RPN: ordinary rates, reduced rates (full medical card or aged 70+, with income of €60,000 or less: 0.5 % then 2 %), or exempt (income up to the €13,000 exemption threshold); ignored on the emergency basis, where USC is 8 % of all pay
Yearly USC rate 1 cut-off from the RPN, if not €12,012
Yearly USC rate 2 cut-off from the RPN, if not €28,700
Yearly USC rate 3 cut-off from the RPN, if not €70,044
Pay to date from previous employments this year, from the RPN (cumulative basis)
Tax deducted to date in previous employments this year, from the RPN
Pay for USC to date from previous employments this year, from the RPN (payForUSCToDate); defaults to previousPay — it differs when pension contributions reduced the previous pay for income tax
USC deducted to date in previous employments this year, from the RPN
Not insurable for PRSI in Ireland (e.g. covered by an A1 certificate from another EU state)

steps.message: Monthly pay must cover a whole calendar month
The cumulative and week 1/month 1 bases need the yearly cut-off point (annualCutOff) and tax credits (annualTaxCredits) from the RPN
Pay under €38 a week (€165 a month) is insured under Class J/M, which this template does not model

limitations: PAYE employment paid weekly or monthly (whole calendar months) in EUR in 2026; the tax year, the tax week or month and the rates are taken from the payment date (Employers' Guide ch. 9). A payment in week 53 (pay day 31 December) uses the week 1 basis figures (Employers' Guide 14.3); pay dated in 2027 is refused. The tax week follows the payment date: where a weekly pay day is moved (e.g. Friday paid on Thursday), the guide (10.2) keeps the normal pay day for the tax week, so enter the normal pay day as the payment date.

Income tax and USC follow the Revenue Payroll Notification entered on the employee: basis, yearly cut-off point and tax credits, USC status and any non-standard USC cut-offs, and pay, tax and USC from previous employments. The template does not fetch or check RPNs; without one, use the emergency basis.

Tax cut-off and credits per period are the yearly figures divided by the periods and rounded up to the cent, multiplied by the tax week or month on the cumulative basis; USC cut-offs per period are rounded to the cent, as in Revenue's examples. The emergency basis gives the first month (or first four weeks of pay) 1/12 (1/52) of the single cut-off and no credits; later periods and the no-PPSN case pay 40 %; USC is 8 % throughout. The first month or four weeks are counted as this employer's pay periods within the tax year (Employers' Guide 14.3); weeks of employment before 1 January are not counted.
Pension and other pre-tax deductions reduce pay for income tax only; USC and PRSI are charged on gross pay.

PRSI is Class A only, worked out per pay period (not cumulatively). Weekly thresholds are the statutory figures, as tabled by the Department of Social Protection; the monthly thresholds (€1,525 / €1,837, credit €52, employer €2,392) are their monthly equivalents (weekly × 52 / 12, rounded to the euro), which the acts leave to 'the equivalent' — the DSP's SW14 guide with the official monthly table could not be retrieved to confirm them. Pay under €38 a week (€165 a month) is refused; employees aged 66 or over receiving the State Pension (Contributory) (Class J), Class S, B, D and other classes, and fortnightly pay, are not modelled.

Statutory sick pay (Sick Leave Act 2022), which the employer pays at 70 % of normal daily earnings up to a daily cap, is not calculated: a leave pay rule only pays a percentage of salary for leave days, and without one approved sick and parental leave is paid as full salary. Maternity Benefit and other Department of Social Protection payments are outside payroll.
The employer rate includes the 1 % National Training Fund levy; reliefs such as the JobsPlus incentive are not modelled.

Not modelled: the reduced USC rate's €60,000 income test (entered via the RPN status), tax exemption and marginal relief (Employers' Guide 9.7), separate periods of employment treated as one (9.6), Local Property Tax deductions shown on the RPN, benefit-in-kind and share-based remuneration.

Status LAW_DERIVED: values are cited from the acts, Revenue's Employers' Guide and USC pages, and the DSP's Class A table; one case reproduces Revenue's weekly tax worked example and one its cumulative refund example.
